pairs.subject: alerting
pairs.evidence: src/lib/alerts.ts:64 Event cooldowns live in process memory and are stamped before sending, so restarts permit duplicates while failed deliveries consume the suppression window.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/alerts-detection.ts:311 Standing-regression sustain removes missing dimension readings before counting consecutive scans, implicitly bridging gaps without a rule-declared no-data policy or an aged not-evaluable state.

src/lib/db/alert-events.ts:76 Cooldown-suppressed event attempts and manual resends create separate history rows; AlertEvent has no episode ownership, acknowledgment, resolution kind, or suppressed-repeat counter.
src/lib/alerts.ts:82 The process-local claim stamps before dispatch and is not released after a failed event send; history is recorded afterward rather than durably governing suppression.

src/lib/alert-delivery.ts:120 Delivery selects the configured tenant/global sink without severity-dependent reach; severity changes message presentation and history, but no routing table or unacknowledged-alert escalation is implemented.
src/lib/scan-alerts.ts:240 The evaluation catch logs an error and returns the same result used when no baseline exists, without persisting or surfacing a failed-evaluation status.

src/lib/maturity/noise.ts:79 The corridor suppresses only when both axes are indecisive: adoption=60 lets a rigor crossing from 51 to 49 announce an ungoverned regression even though the changing input remains inside the noise corridor.

src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts:293 Flat recipients are counted and returned without a durable per-recipient outcome; no-channel, no-data and deadline skips likewise lack records distinguishing a skipped edition from an unexecuted run.

src/lib/db/org-alerts.ts:64 The API validates thresholds as integers within 1..100, but the storage setter accepts unchecked numbers, contrary to the required storage-boundary validation door; the editor also lacks historical firing previews.

pairs.registryProposal: Clarify dedup-and-cooldown's final requirement for recovery notifications to have separate suppression state: earlier text requires opposite-direction pushes at the same reach to consume one shared pool, so the final rule should distinguish quiet recovery from full-reach recovery.
